date.as_written: aṣṭḥā(!)daśāṃkeṃduśāke māse madhau stathā(!) mūlakṣye(!) bhaṃ || yogavyatiś ca navami(!) asitās(!)tathā ... saumyavāsare

notes: The chronogram aṣṭādaśa (18) + aṅka (9) + indu (1) is to be read left to right as ŚS 1891. With the usual right-to-left rule it would give ŚS 1918 (1996 CE), which is very likely too late for an A-series NGMCP reel. ŚS 1891 checks out astronomically: Caitra kṛṣṇa navamī counted pūrṇimānta (the dark half after Phālguna pūrṇimā, 4 March 1969) falls on 12 March 1969, a Wednesday (saumya = Budha). That day the Moon was in mūla and the yoga was vyatīpāta (sidereal Sun about 327° + Moon about 249° ≈ 216°). This agrees with the catalogue's tentative '1891?'. The pūrṇimānta month naming suggests a Maithili scribe. The scribe's name is corrupt: 'bhavanāthadvijaskasya' is probably for bhavanāthadvijasya, or dvijakasya with a -ka suffix. This does not affect the name Bhavanātha. 'yogavyatiś' = vyatīpāta yoga; 'mūlakṣye bhaṃ' = mūlarkṣe bham (nakṣatra mūla).
